relevance_note: A family case report with three carriers of a TNFAIP3 missense VUS: 'The proband, his daughter, and his sister who are all affected with chronic urticaria and angioedema each carry the c.65G>A (p.R22Q) variant inTNFAIP3.'
method_note: Hand extraction, JSON assembled by a short Python script from hand-chosen spans; no tables in the paper. The paper has no own labels: the proband is 'patient' (rule 5, the single index patient of the case report; 'the proband' is a role word), relatives labelled by relation. The mother is in scope as a tested relative (TNFAIP3-negative); she carries the GJB2 c.35del variant, so she has a GJB2 row but no TNFAIP3 row. The father ('the proband's father was deceased') was neither tested nor described as affected and has no row. Further relatives in the pedigree figure are not described in text. No HA20 diagnosis is made: the authors classify the TNFAIP3 variant as a VUS and the phenotype is chronic urticaria with angioedema. Sister: parental testing statement left not reported because the paper tests 'the proband's mother' and does not say she is also the sister's mother. Daughter: inheritance recorded as 'inherited paternal' because the paper states her father (the proband) carries the same variant. Proband GJB2 inheritance 'inherited maternal' because the variant is found 'in the proband and his mother only'; proband GJB2 zygosity not stated for him and left not reported. GJB2 variant printed as c.35del (Results) and c.35delG (Conclusion); c.35del recorded. Normal findings (bone marrow biopsy, CBC, mast cell panel, SPEP) are recorded as excluded abnormalities at the level the paper names; normal TSH is recorded as 'abnormal TSH' excluded and does not exclude autoimmune thyroiditis. The normal CBC with differential was used to mark cytopenia excluded for the proband. The elevated anti-IgE receptor antibody was not counted as checklist 'autoantibodies' because the paper does not call it an autoantibody. Molecular modelling (in silico) is not recorded as functional evidence; the paper says functional analyses are still needed. Urticaria/hives counted as checklist skin lesions (rash). Onset 'early 30s' has no ISO value because the number is approximate. No contradictions found within the paper.
